Are you a small business owner struggling to get noticed online? You’ve invested in your business, built a great product or service, and now you need customers. One of the most effective and affordable ways to do that is through Bing Places for Business.

Bing Places for Business (formerly Bing Places) is a free tool that allows you to manage your business’s online presence on Bing. It’s a critical component of your local SEO strategy, often overlooked in favor of Google Business Profile. While Google dominates the search market, Bing still holds a significant share - approximately 16 percent of all searches in the USA, according to a recent analysis.

The first step is to claim your business listing. Here’s a breakdown of the process: 1. Go to Bing Places for Business: Navigate to 2. Sign In: Use your Microsoft account (the same one you use for Outlook, Hotmail, or Xbox). If you don’t have one, create one. Search for Your Business: Type your business name into the search bar.

Once your listing is claimed, it’s time to fill out the details. This is where you’ll truly optimize your listing for local search. Business Name: Ensure this is exactly as it appears on your signage and other marketing materials. Consistency across platforms is vital for customer recognition. Address: Provide your full street address, including the city, state, and zip code.

Regularly update these hours, especially during holidays or special events. Category: Select the most relevant category for your business. For example, instead of “Restaurant,” choose “Italian Restaurant” or “Mexican Restaurant.” A more specific category helps Bing understand your business and target the right audience. Description: Write a compelling and informative description of your business. Include what you offer, your unique selling points, and any special promotions.

Break down your offerings into specific services or products. This helps customers find exactly what they’re looking for. For example, if you’re a pizza restaurant, list each pizza type, toppings, and sizes. If you’re a hair salon, list the specific services you offer (e.g., haircuts, coloring, styling). The more detail you provide, the better you can cater to customer needs.

Proactively asking for reviews from satisfied customers is a powerful strategy. Regularly update your business information to ensure accuracy. This includes your hours, address, phone number, website, and any other details. Outdated information can negatively impact your ranking. Set a reminder to review your listing at least once a month. Bing Places actively monitors for changes, so staying on top of updates is crucial.

Direction Requests: Track how many people are requesting directions to your business. This shows how many people are considering visiting your location. Views: Monitor how many times your listing is viewed. This provides a general sense of interest in your business. Incorrect Information: Double-check all details for accuracy. Even small errors can hurt your ranking. Missing Information: Don’t leave any fields blank.

By following the steps outlined here, you can increase your visibility in Bing search results, drive more traffic to your business, and ultimately, boost your sales.
